```{r global, include=FALSE}
library (flexdashboard)
library (readr)
dataset <- read_csv("dataset.csv")

percent <- function(number){
  return(number/nrow(dataset)*100)
}

intl <- function(target){
  return(dataset$International == 1 & dataset$Target == target)
}

colour = c("brown","blue")
  
#local <- function(target){
 #amt2 = sum(dataset$International == 0 & dataset$Target == target)
 #return (amt2)
#}

```

# General {data-icon="fa-user"}

## Column 1

### Enrolled

```{r}
enrolled = sum(dataset$Target == "Enrolled")
valueBox(enrolled,icon = "fa-pencil",col = "skyblue")

```

### Enrolled

```{r}
enrolled_per = percent(enrolled)

gauge(enrolled_per, min = 0, max = 100, symbol = '%', gaugeSectors(
  success = c(80, 100), warning = c(40, 79), danger = c(0, 39)
))
```

### Statistics

```{r}
#en_intl = intl("Enrolled")
#en_local = local("Enrolled")

en_stat <- table(intl("Enrolled"))
text(x = barplot(en_stat,beside = TRUE, names = c("Local","International"),col=colour), label = en_stat, pos = 3, cex = 0.8, col = "black")

# Specify the range and number of ticks for the y-axis
axis(side = 2, at = pretty(range(nrow(dataset)), n = 5))

```

# Category {data-icon="fa-graduation-cap"}

## Column 1 {.sidebar}

```{r}
selectInput(inputId = "gender_choice", label = "Gender:",
              choices = c("Male", "Female"), selected = "Male")

selectInput("course_name", label = "Course:",
              choices = c(dataset$Course), selected = 0)

sliderInput(
  inputId = "age_adjust", label = "Age at enrollment:",
  min = 15, max = 70, value = 1, step = 1
)

```

## Column 2

### No. of dropouts

```{r}
### No. of dropouts vs Gender, Course, and Age at enrollment
renderPlot({
  # Ensure all required inputs are available
  req(input$gender_choice, input$course_name, input$age_adjust)
  
  # Convert input$gender_choice to 0 for Female and 1 for Male
  gender_num <- ifelse(input$gender_choice == "Female", 0, 1)
  
  # Define all possible categories
  categories <- c("Dropout", "Enrolled", "Graduate")
  
  # Initialize counts for all categories to zero
  counts <- rep(0, length(categories))
  
  # Subset the dataset based on all three conditions
  subset_data <- dataset[dataset$Gender == gender_num & 
                        dataset$Course == input$course_name & 
                        dataset$`Age at enrollment` == input$age_adjust, ]
  
  # Calculate the counts for each category from the subset data
  subset_counts <- table(subset_data$Target)
  
  # Match the subset counts with the predefined categories
  counts[match(names(subset_counts), categories)] <- subset_counts
  
  # Calculate the maximum count among all categories for y-axis scaling
  max_count <- max(counts)
  
  # Check if counts is empty or contains only NA values
  if (sum(counts) == 0) {
    # If counts is empty or contains only NA values, show a message
    plot(0, type = "n", xlab = "Category", ylab = "Count", main = "Number of each category")
    text(0, 0, "No data available", col = "red", cex = 1.5)
  } else {
    # Calculate suitable xlim based on the number of categories
    num_categories <- length(categories)
    xlim <- c(0.2, num_categories + 1)  # Add padding for better visualization
  
    # Create bar plot
    barplot(counts, 
            main = "No. of Dropouts vs Gender, Course, and Age",
            xlab = "Category",
            ylab = "Count",
            col = c("salmon", "skyblue", "lightgreen"),  # Customize colors based on "Target" variable
            ylim = c(0, max_count * 1.1), 
            xlim = xlim,
            beside = TRUE,
            names = c("Dropout","Enrolled","Graduated")
            )
    
    # Add data labels to the bars
    text(x = 1:num_categories, y = counts, labels = counts, pos = 3, cex = 0.8, col = "black")
  }
}, width = 450, height = 550)  # Set width and height to control the size of the plot area



```

## Column 3

### No. of dropouts vs Gender

```{r}
renderPlot({
  req(input$gender_choice)  # Ensure input$gender_choice is available
  
  # Convert input$gender_choice to 0 for Female and 1 for Male
  gender_num <- ifelse(input$gender_choice == "Female", 0, 1)
  
  # Subset the dataset based on the converted gender choice
  gender_subset <- dataset[dataset$Gender == gender_num, c("Gender", "Target")]
  
  # Create a table of counts for the "Target" variable (e.g., Dropout, Enrolled, Graduate)
  gender_counts <- table(gender_subset$Target)
  
  # Create a bar plot of the counts
  barplot(gender_counts, 
          main = paste("Number of", input$gender_choice, "in Each Category"),
          ylab = "Count",
          col = c("salmon","skyblue","lightgreen"),  # Set color of bars
          ylim = c(0, max(gender_counts) * 2),  # Set y-axis limits to ensure all bars are visible
          beside = TRUE)  # Display bars side by side
  
  # Add data labels to the bars
  text(x = 1:length(gender_counts), y = gender_counts, labels = gender_counts, pos = 3, cex = 0.8, col = "black")
})

```

### No. of dropouts vs Age at enrollment

```{r}
renderPlot({
  req(input$age_adjust)  # Ensure input$course_name is available
  
  # Define all possible categories
  categories <- c("Dropout", "Enrolled", "Graduate")
  
  # Initialize counts for all categories to zero
  counts <- rep(0, length(categories))
  
  # Subset the dataset based on the converted gender choice
  age_subset <- dataset[dataset$`Age at enrollment` == input$age_adjust, c("Age at enrollment", "Target")]
  
  # Calculate the counts for each category from the subset data
  subset_counts <- table(age_subset$Target)
  
  # Match the subset counts with the predefined categories
  counts[match(names(subset_counts), categories)] <- subset_counts
  
  # Check if counts is empty or contains only NA values
  if (sum(counts) == 0) {
    # If counts is empty or contains only NA values, show a message
    plot(0, type = "n", xlab = "Category", ylab = "Count", main = "Number of each category")
    text(0, 0, "No data available", col = "red", cex = 1.5)
  } else {
    # Calculate suitable xlim based on the number of categories
    num_categories <- length(categories)
    xlim <- c(0.2, num_categories + 1)  # Add padding for better visualization
    
    # Create a bar plot of the counts
    barplot(counts, 
            main = paste("Number of", input$age_adjust, "year-old in Each Category"),
            ylab = "Count",
            col = c("salmon","skyblue","lightgreen"),  # Set color of bars
            ylim = c(0.2, max(counts) * 2),  # Set y-axis limits to ensure all bars are visible
            xlim = xlim,
            beside = TRUE,  # Display bars side by side
            names = c("Dropout","Enrolled","Graduated")) 
    # Add data labels to the bars
    text(x = 1:num_categories, y = counts, labels = counts, pos = 3, cex = 0.8, col = "black")
  }
})

```
